metadata.name: Personal Development Memory
metadata.description: Simulated developer activity over 3 months - conversations with AI coding assistants, git commits, code reviews, configuration changes. Tests understanding of coding philosophy, style patterns, and problem-solving approaches.

learners.name: Generic Developer Memory
learners.purpose: Understand core development philosophy, coding style patterns, and recurring problem-solving approaches

learners.name: Philosophy Specialist
learners.purpose: Understand the developer's core beliefs about software engineering - what they value, what they avoid, and why

learners.name: Code Style Specialist
learners.purpose: Track coding style patterns - naming conventions, formatting preferences, structural choices, and code organization

learners.name: Tooling Specialist
learners.purpose: Understand tool preferences - libraries, frameworks, testing tools, linters, and development environment choices

queries: What testing practices do I follow?
Do I prefer OOP or functional?
What are my thoughts on abstractions?
How do I approach code reviews?

events.user_message: I'm starting a new API project. Should I use NestJS or just plain Express?
events.assistant_response: For a new API, both are valid choices...
events.user_followup: I think I'll go with plain Express. NestJS feels over-engineered for what I need. I can add structure as I go.

events.message: chore: init project with minimal express setup

events.user_message: What folder structure do you recommend?
events.user_followup: I'll start flat and extract when patterns emerge. Premature structure is as bad as premature optimization.

events.message: feat: add user registration endpoint

events.comment: This abstracts too early. We only have 3 routes. Just add console.log where needed and extract a middleware when we have 10+ routes.

events.user_message: How should I handle errors in Express routes?
events.assistant_response: You can use try/catch, error middleware, or Result types...
events.user_followup: I'll use explicit returns. throw feels like goto. If a function can fail, I want it in the return type.

events.message: feat: add Result type for explicit error handling

events.change: Set strict: true, noImplicitAny: true, strictNullChecks: true

events.user_message: What's the best validation library?
events.assistant_response: Popular options include Joi, Yup, Zod...
events.user_followup: Zod looks good. TypeScript-first, infers types automatically. One source of truth for runtime and compile-time validation.

events.message: refactor: use zod schemas for request validation

events.user_message: Should I write unit tests or integration tests first?
events.assistant_response: Testing pyramid suggests unit tests at base...
events.user_followup: I'll focus on integration tests for APIs. Unit tests for pure functions only. Testing implementation details is a waste of time.

events.message: test: add integration tests for user registration

events.comment: Why a class? This has no state. Just export functions. Classes should only exist when you need encapsulated state.

events.user_message: Postgres or MongoDB for this project?
events.user_followup: Postgres. Relational data, ACID transactions, and I actually know my schema. NoSQL is for when you don't know your data model yet.

events.message: feat: add postgres connection with raw SQL

events.user_message: Should I use Prisma or TypeORM?
events.user_followup: Neither for now. Raw SQL with a thin wrapper. ORMs add magic I don't need yet. If queries get complex, I'll add Kysely.

events.comment: Repository pattern for 2 tables? This is enterprise cosplay. Just use the query functions directly.

events.message: refactor: simplify db layer, remove unnecessary abstractions

events.user_message: camelCase or snake_case for API responses?
events.assistant_response: JavaScript convention is camelCase, but some prefer snake_case for APIs...
events.user_followup: camelCase everywhere. One convention, no translation layers. The API is consumed by JS clients anyway.

events.message: feat: add authentication with JWT

events.user_message: Where should I store JWT tokens on the client?
events.assistant_response: Options include localStorage, sessionStorage, httpOnly cookies...
events.user_followup: httpOnly cookies. Never trust client-side storage with auth tokens. XSS is too easy.

events.change: Set printWidth: 100, useTabs: true, singleQuote: true
events.reason: Tabs for accessibility, single quotes for consistency

events.pr: PR #22 - Add comments to all functions
events.comment: These comments just repeat the function name. 'getUserById gets a user by ID' - I can read. Remove noise, add comments only for non-obvious behavior.

events.user_message: What logging library should I use?
events.assistant_response: Popular options include Winston, Pino, Bunyan...
events.user_followup: Pino. Fastest, JSON by default, minimal API. Winston is bloated. I just need structured logs to stdout.

events.message: feat: add request logging middleware

events.user_message: How detailed should error messages be?
events.user_followup: Different for dev and prod. Dev: full stack traces. Prod: error codes with correlation IDs. Never leak internals to users.

events.message: feat: add error response formatting with correlation IDs

events.comment: Good. But rename 'handleException' to 'handleError'. Exceptions are a Java concept. In JS we handle errors.

events.user_message: How long should a function be?
events.assistant_response: Some say under 20 lines, others focus on single responsibility...
events.user_followup: No magic number. A function should do one thing. If I can't name it clearly, it's doing too much. If it needs comments explaining sections, split it.

events.message: refactor: split large registration handler into steps

events.user_message: I have similar code in two places. Should I extract it?
events.user_followup: Not yet. Duplication is cheaper than the wrong abstraction. Wait until I see it three times and understand the pattern.

events.comment: These validations are only 'similar', not identical. Different contexts, different requirements. Keep them separate until they truly converge.

events.message: feat: add password reset flow

events.user_message: Should I use a template engine for emails?
events.assistant_response: Options include Handlebars, EJS, or React Email...
events.user_followup: Template literals for now. Only 2 email types. I'll add React Email if we get to 10+ templates.

events.user_message: How should I version my API?
events.assistant_response: Common approaches include URL path, header, query param...
events.user_followup: URL path (/v1/). Clear, cacheable, obvious. Header versioning is clever but clients hate it.

events.message: refactor: add /v1 prefix to all routes

events.comment: Why GraphQL? We have 5 REST endpoints. GraphQL adds complexity with no benefit at this scale. Solve problems you have, not problems you imagine.

events.user_message: Should I use a DI container?
events.user_followup: No container needed. Just pass dependencies as function arguments. If that gets unwieldy, I'll reconsider. Most DI libraries are overkill for non-enterprise apps.

events.message: feat: add rate limiting middleware

events.user_message: Redis or in-memory for rate limiting?
events.assistant_response: Redis for distributed, in-memory for single instance...
events.user_followup: In-memory. Single instance for now. I'll add Redis when we scale horizontally. YAGNI until then.

events.comment: We're not at scale where this matters. Add it when response times are actually a problem. Premature caching creates invalidation bugs.

events.message: test: add load tests with k6

events.user_message: When should I run load tests?
events.user_followup: Before production and after major changes. Not in CI for every commit - too slow. Have a separate performance pipeline.

events.message: feat: add health check endpoint

events.user_message: What should a health check include?
events.assistant_response: Options include simple ping, database check, dependency checks...
events.user_followup: Two endpoints: /health (always 200, for LB), /health/deep (checks DB, for monitoring). Separate concerns.

events.comment: Good Dockerfile. But remove the dev dependencies from the image. Production images should be minimal.

events.message: chore: optimize Docker image with multi-stage build

events.user_message: How should I handle environment variables?
events.assistant_response: Use .env files, config libraries like dotenv...
events.user_followup: Validate at startup with zod. If required config is missing, fail fast with clear error. Don't let the app start in bad state.

events.message: feat: add config validation on startup

events.user_message: Callbacks, promises, or async/await?
events.user_followup: async/await everywhere. Promises when composing. Never callbacks unless forced by old library. Consistency is key.

events.pr: PR #50 - Refactor to use callbacks for performance
events.comment: The performance difference is nanoseconds. Readability matters more. Keep async/await unless you profile and prove it's a bottleneck.

events.message: feat: add database migrations

events.user_message: What migration tool should I use?
events.assistant_response: Options include Knex migrations, Prisma migrate...
events.user_followup: Plain SQL files with a simple runner. I want to see and version the exact DDL. Migration tools add magic.

events.comment: Good. But wrap the transaction logic in a helper that handles begin/commit/rollback. Reduces boilerplate.

events.message: refactor: add transaction helper function

events.user_message: When is it okay to use 'as' type assertions?
events.assistant_response: When you know more than the compiler...
events.user_followup: Almost never. If I need 'as', usually means I should fix the types. Only exception: test mocks where I'm intentionally partial.

events.reason: Arrays should be checked before access. Prevents undefined bugs.

events.message: feat: add user profile endpoints

events.user_message: Singular or plural for REST resources?
events.user_followup: Plural. /users, /posts, /comments. Consistent and matches the collection concept. Exception: /me for current user.

events.comment: Soft deletes add complexity. Do we actually need to restore data? If yes, proceed. If 'maybe someday', just delete. We have backups.

events.user_message: Should I implement soft deletes?
events.user_followup: Only for things with legal/compliance requirements. For user data, yes. For temporary resources like sessions, hard delete.

events.message: feat: add soft delete for users with audit trail

events.user_message: Should I use interface or type in TypeScript?
events.assistant_response: Interfaces are extendable, types are more flexible...
events.user_followup: type for data shapes, interface for contracts that might be implemented. In practice, type for almost everything.

events.comment: Not needed. Types are fine for DTOs and response shapes. Save interfaces for when you need declaration merging or class contracts.

events.message: feat: add pagination to list endpoints

events.user_message: Offset or cursor pagination?
events.assistant_response: Offset is simpler, cursor is more efficient for large datasets...
events.user_followup: Cursor. Offset breaks on real-time data and gets slow at scale. Start with cursor, never have to migrate later.

events.message: refactor: switch to cursor-based pagination

events.comment: Good idea. But generate from code, don't manually maintain. Code is source of truth. Spec should be derived.

events.user_message: How should I document the API?
events.user_followup: Generate OpenAPI from schemas. Self-documenting. Manual docs drift from reality. If the schema changes, docs update automatically.

events.message: feat: auto-generate OpenAPI spec from Zod schemas

events.user_message: Should I add feature flags?
events.user_followup: Not until we have a feature that needs gradual rollout. Environment-based config suffices for now. Feature flags are infrastructure debt.

events.comment: We're 3 developers. Talk to each other. Feature flags solve coordination problems at scale we don't have.

events.message: feat: add webhook support for user events

events.user_message: Should I use an event bus like RabbitMQ?
events.user_followup: HTTP webhooks first. Simpler, debuggable, no infrastructure. Event bus when we have multiple consumers or need guaranteed delivery.

events.comment: We have one service with 10 endpoints. Microservices solve distribution problems. We have a complexity problem. Monolith first.

events.user_message: When should we move to microservices?
events.user_followup: When team boundaries require service boundaries. Or when a component needs different scaling/deployment. Never for 'good architecture' alone.

events.message: refactor: organize monolith by feature, not layer

events.user_message: Should I organize by layer (routes, handlers, models) or by feature?
events.user_followup: Feature. When I work on users, I want all user code together. Layer organization means jumping between folders constantly.

events.comment: What's 'shared'? If it's used everywhere, it's a library. If it's used by 2 features, put it in one and import. 'Shared' folders become junk drawers.

events.message: refactor: move truly shared code to lib/

events.user_message: What observability stack do you recommend?
events.assistant_response: Options include Datadog, New Relic, open-source stacks...
events.user_followup: Logs, metrics, traces. Start with structured logs (Pino). Add Prometheus metrics when we need dashboards. Traces when debugging distributed calls.

events.message: feat: add prometheus metrics endpoint

events.comment: Too many metrics. Focus on RED: Rate, Errors, Duration. Add others when we have specific questions to answer.

events.user_message: What security headers should I add?
events.assistant_response: Common headers include CORS, CSP, HSTS...
events.user_followup: Use Helmet.js but understand each header. Don't just copy defaults. CSP needs to match actual resources we load.

events.message: feat: add security headers with customized CSP

events.user_message: What code coverage should I target?
events.user_followup: Coverage is vanity. Focus on testing behavior, not lines. 100% coverage with bad tests is worse than 60% with good ones.

events.pr: PR #84 - Add tests to reach 80% coverage
events.comment: Some of these tests just exercise code without asserting behavior. Remove the getter tests. Add tests for edge cases we missed.

events.message: test: add edge case tests, remove trivial coverage tests

events.user_message: When should I mock in tests?
events.user_followup: Mock what you don't own: external APIs, databases in unit tests. Never mock your own code - that tests implementation, not behavior.

events.pr: PR #87 - Mock database in handler tests
events.comment: These are integration tests. Use a real test database. Mocking the DB defeats the purpose - we want to test actual queries.

events.message: chore: add test database setup with docker-compose

events.user_message: GitHub Actions or CircleCI?
events.user_followup: GitHub Actions. We're on GitHub, native integration, good enough for our needs. Simpler than managing another service.

events.message: ci: add GitHub Actions workflow

events.comment: Good start. But separate build and deploy stages. Build artifact should be immutable - same artifact to staging and production.

events.user_message: Kubernetes or simpler?
events.user_followup: Fly.io or Railway. We're a small app. K8s operational overhead doesn't make sense until we have dedicated infra team.

events.message: chore: add fly.io configuration

events.user_message: GitFlow or trunk-based?
events.assistant_response: GitFlow for releases, trunk-based for continuous...
events.user_followup: Trunk-based. Short-lived feature branches, direct to main. GitFlow is for enterprises with release trains. We ship continuously.

events.comment: We don't need develop. Main is always deployable. Feature branches merge to main. Adding branches adds ceremony, not safety.

events.user_message: How thorough should code reviews be?
events.user_followup: Focus on: logic errors, security issues, unclear code. Don't bikeshed naming or style - that's what linters are for. Ship fast, fix forward.

events.message: feat: add admin endpoints with role-based access

events.user_message: RBAC or ABAC?
events.assistant_response: RBAC is simpler, ABAC more flexible...
events.user_followup: RBAC for now. We have 3 roles. ABAC adds complexity we don't need. Can migrate if requirements grow.

events.comment: CASL is overkill for 3 roles. A simple middleware checking role is enough. Libraries solve problems, not check boxes.

events.message: feat: add simple role-based middleware

events.user_message: date-fns or dayjs?
events.assistant_response: Both are good, date-fns is tree-shakeable...
events.user_followup: date-fns. Tree-shaking matters for bundle. Only import functions I use. dayjs requires full library.

events.comment: Moment is deprecated and huge. Use date-fns or native Intl. Stop adding legacy libraries.

events.user_message: Should I use null or undefined?
events.user_followup: undefined for absence, null for intentional empty. In practice: avoid both with proper types. Optional chaining and nullish coalescing help.

events.message: refactor: replace null checks with optional chaining

events.pr: PR #102 - Add utility functions for null checks
events.comment: TypeScript has optional chaining and nullish coalescing. Native features > utility functions.

events.user_message: What would you change about this project?
events.user_followup: Started about right. Kept it simple, added complexity only when needed. Main regret: should have added cursor pagination earlier. Retrofitting was painful.

events.user_message: I keep making the same abstraction mistake. How do I learn?
events.user_followup: The pattern: I want to 'do it right' so I abstract early. Then requirements change and abstraction doesn't fit. Lesson: write the thing three times, then extract.

events.user_message: We have some legacy code from before I joined. Rewrite or refactor?
events.assistant_response: Depends on the scope and risk...
events.user_followup: Strangle fig pattern. Add tests first. Replace piece by piece. Big rewrites fail. Incremental improvement wins.

events.comment: This is a full rewrite with no tests. Add integration tests first to capture current behavior. Then refactor with safety net.

events.user_message: How do you manage technical debt?
events.user_followup: TODO comments for small stuff. Issues for bigger stuff. But most importantly: fix it when you're in the file. Don't plan debt cleanup sprints.

events.user_message: How do you establish coding standards in a team?
events.user_followup: Automate everything possible. Linters for style, types for correctness. Discussions for design patterns. Never argue about things a tool can check.

events.comment: Good initiative, but most of this is enforceable by biome. Convert to rules, not prose. Docs get ignored, linter errors don't.

events.message: chore: add strict biome rules replacing style guide

events.user_message: Looking back at 3 months, what are my main patterns?
events.user_followup: Simplicity over cleverness. Types over tests (both matter, types catch more). Explicit over implicit. Native over library when possible. Ship, then improve.

events.comment: Good quarter. Code is simpler than when we started. That's rare - usually codebases only grow complex. Well done team.

events.message: docs: update README with current architecture

events.user_message: Best practices for variable naming?
events.user_followup: Names should explain what, not how. 'filteredUsers' good, 'loopResult' bad. If I need a comment to explain a name, the name is wrong.

events.comment: Good change. 'data' -> 'userProfile', 'res' -> 'apiResponse'. Specific is always better than generic.

events.user_message: How should I name boolean variables?
events.assistant_response: Use prefixes like is, has, should...
events.user_followup: is/has/can/should prefix for booleans. 'active' is ambiguous. 'isActive' is clear. Exception: obvious booleans like 'visible', 'enabled'.

events.message: refactor: standardize boolean naming with is/has prefixes

events.user_message: What about function naming conventions?
events.assistant_response: Verbs for actions, nouns for getters...
events.user_followup: Verb for actions (createUser, deletePost), adjective for transformers (formatted, validated), question for predicates (isEmpty, hasAccess).

events.comment: Good. 'process' -> 'normalizeInput', 'handle' -> 'routeRequest'. Generic verbs are code smells.

events.user_message: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE for constants?
events.user_followup: Only for true constants: MAX_RETRIES, API_TIMEOUT. Not for config values that could change. Regular camelCase for those.

events.message: refactor: fix constant naming conventions

events.user_message: How should I organize imports?
events.user_followup: External packages first, then internal. Let the linter sort within groups. Don't waste mental energy on import order.

events.comment: Remove manual import organization. Enable biome's import sorter. Never manually do what tools can automate.

events.user_message: Should I use early returns or single return?
events.user_followup: Early returns always. Guard clauses at the top, happy path at the bottom. Deeply nested if/else is unreadable.

events.message: refactor: convert nested conditions to early returns

events.pr: PR #42 - Add else blocks for clarity
events.comment: This adds visual noise. After 'if (invalid) return error', the next line is implicitly the valid case. No else needed.

events.user_message: When are ternary operators okay?
events.user_followup: Single line, simple values only. condition ? valueA : valueB. Never nested ternaries. If it needs multiple lines, use if/else.

events.comment: The nested ternary on line 45 is unreadable. Convert to if/else or early returns. Clever code is not good code.

events.user_message: Best practices for destructuring?
events.user_followup: Destructure at point of use, not at function start. Only destructure what you need. Deep destructuring is a smell - flatten your data.

events.pr: PR #61 - Destructure all params at start
events.comment: This destructures 12 fields, uses 3. Only destructure what you need, where you need it.

events.message: refactor: clean up excessive destructuring

events.user_message: When to use spread vs Object.assign?
events.user_followup: Spread for shallow copies: { ...obj, newProp }. Object.assign only for mutating in place, which I avoid anyway. Immutability by default.

events.comment: Use spread: { ...defaults, ...overrides }. Clearer than Object.assign, same result, immutable.

events.user_message: Any advice for developers starting out?
events.user_followup: Write code. Delete code. Shipping beats planning. Types catch bugs, tests verify behavior. Simple code lives longer. The best code is code you don't write.

events.message: chore: Q1 complete - tag v1.0.0

events.comment: From 0 to production in 3 months. Clean code, comprehensive tests, simple architecture. This is how software should be built. Ship it.

events.user_message: v1.0 is live. What's the most important thing I learned?
events.user_followup: Simplicity is a feature. Every line of code is a liability. The goal isn't to write code, it's to solve problems. Sometimes the best solution is not writing code at all.
